jobs.title: Bioinformatics Scientist / Senior Bioinformatics Scientist — cfDNA-Based Cancer Screening
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Bioinformatics Scientist or Senior Bioinformatics Scientist to develop, optimize, validate, and maintain bioinformatics pipelines for a cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening assay.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational biology, next-generation sequencing (NGS), molecular diagnostics, and statistical modeling. This individual will be responsible for transforming raw sequencing data into reliable analytical outputs and developing robust computational methods to identify cancer-associated molecular signals in plasma-derived cfDNA.

The role will support analytical validation, algorithm development, assay performance optimization, and preparation for clinical and regulatory submissions. The candidate will collaborate closely with molecular biology, assay development, laboratory automation, clinical, quality, and regulatory teams to establish a reproducible, scalable, and well-documented bioinformatics workflow.

Key Responsibilities

1. NGS Bioinformatics Pipeline Development

Develop, optimize, and maintain end-to-end bioinformatics pipelines for cfDNA-based targeted sequencing assays.
Process and analyze raw sequencing data, including FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, and VCF or other assay-specific intermediate files.
Implement quality control metrics for sequencing quality, mapping, coverage, library complexity, molecular error rates, and sample-level performance.
Develop methods for low-frequency variant detection, error suppression, background-noise characterization, and identification of cancer-associated molecular features, as appropriate to the assay design.
Optimize computational workflows for throughput, reproducibility, scalability, and efficient processing of high-volume sequencing data.
Integrate bioinformatics outputs with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), automated laboratory workflows, and downstream reporting systems as needed.

2. Algorithm and Biomarker Development

Develop and evaluate computational methods to identify cancer-associated signals in cfDNA, including genomic alterations and other molecular features supported by the assay design.
Collaborate with molecular biologists and assay scientists to investigate biological and technical sources of background noise.
Develop statistical models and classification algorithms to distinguish cancer-associated signals from non-cancer background.
Evaluate feature selection, model training, cross-validation, threshold optimization, and generalizability using appropriate study designs.
Assess the effects of cfDNA input, sequencing depth, tumor fraction, sample quality, and pre-analytical variables on algorithm performance.
Maintain clear separation between model development, parameter tuning, and independent performance evaluation to minimize overfitting and data leakage.

3. Bioinformatics Analytical Validation

Design and execute bioinformatics validation studies in collaboration with assay development and analytical validation teams.
Establish and document software and algorithm performance characteristics, including:
Analytical accuracy and reproducibility.
Detection performance across relevant signal levels.
False-positive and false-negative analytical calls.
Robustness to sequencing depth, input variability, and technical noise.
Sample-level quality control and failure criteria.
Computational precision, deterministic behavior, and reproducibility across software versions.
Evaluate the impact of sequencing errors, contamination, sample mix-ups, batch effects, and other potential confounders.
Define acceptance criteria, validation datasets, statistical analysis plans, and validation reports before study execution.
Support investigations of discrepant results, pipeline failures, and unexpected assay performance.

4. Software Engineering and Computational Infrastructure

Develop maintainable, modular, and version-controlled bioinformatics software using Python, R, and/or other appropriate programming languages.
Implement workflow management using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake, or WDL.
Use Git-based version control, automated testing, continuous integration, containers, and reproducible software environments.
Deploy workflows in cloud or high-performance computing environments, as appropriate.
Establish automated quality checks, audit-friendly execution logs, data lineage, version tracking, and monitoring.
Develop unit, integration, regression, and end-to-end tests to ensure reliable pipeline performance.
Collaborate with software engineering and IT teams to maintain secure and reliable computational infrastructure.

5. Clinical Performance and Translational Research Support

Support retrospective and prospective studies evaluating cfDNA-based cancer screening algorithms.
Collaborate with biostatisticians and clinical scientists to assess sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and other clinical performance measures.
Support the development of independent training, tuning, and test datasets for algorithm development and evaluation.
Analyze discordant cases and investigate associations between molecular features, clinical findings, and reference-standard outcomes.
Support clinical study data analysis, technical documentation, and preparation of scientific publications and presentations.

6. Regulatory, Quality, and Documentation

Prepare technical documentation for analytical validation, software verification and validation, design controls, and regulatory submissions.
Work with Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs to ensure compliance with applicable requirements for clinical laboratory testing and in vitro diagnostic software.
Maintain traceability between software requirements, risk controls, test cases, validation evidence, and software releases.
Contribute to change-control procedures, risk assessments, deviation investigations, and corrective and preventive actions when applicable.
Support the development of controlled procedures for pipeline deployment, updates, maintenance, and release approval.

7. Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with assay development, molecular biology, laboratory operations, automation engineering, biostatistics, clinical development, and regulatory teams.
Translate biological and clinical questions into computational analyses and actionable technical requirements.
Communicate complex bioinformatics findings clearly to scientific and non-computational stakeholders.
Contribute to experimental design, assay optimization, troubleshooting, and strategic development of the cancer screening platform.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Biostatistics, Computer Science, or a related discipline; alternatively, an M.S. with substantial relevant industry experience.
Strong experience analyzing NGS data, preferably from targeted sequencing assays or liquid biopsy applications.
Proficiency in Python and/or R, including experience developing reusable, well-tested analytical code.
Demonstrated understanding of NGS data processing, sequencing quality control, alignment, variant calling, and statistical analysis.
Experience with Linux/Unix environments, shell scripting, Git, and reproducible computational workflows.
Strong knowledge of statistical methods, experimental design, data quality assessment, and performance evaluation.
Ability to independently troubleshoot complex computational problems and communicate results across multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with cfDNA, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), liquid biopsy, or blood-based cancer screening assays.
Experience with ultra-low-frequency variant detection, molecular barcodes or unique molecular identifiers (UMIs), error-corrected sequencing, and sequencing background suppression.
Familiarity with machine learning, predictive modeling, classification algorithms, and evaluation of clinical biomarkers.
Experience developing or validating bioinformatics pipelines for oncology or clinical diagnostics.
Knowledge of analytical validation concepts, including limit of blank, limit of detection, precision, interference, reproducibility, and robustness.
Experience with Nextflow, Snakemake, Docker, Singularity/Apptainer, cloud computing, or high-performance computing.
Familiarity with regulated software development, design controls, software risk management, and relevant FDA and CLSI guidance.
Experience integrating sequencing workflows with LIMS, laboratory automation platforms, or clinical reporting systems.
Experience supporting clinical studies, regulatory submissions, or commercialization of molecular diagnostic assays.

Key Deliverables and Measures of Success

During the first 6–12 months, the successful candidate is expected to:
Establish or improve a reproducible end-to-end NGS bioinformatics pipeline for the cfDNA-based CRC screening assay.
Implement documented sample-level and sequencing-level quality control metrics and failure criteria.
Develop or optimize the assay-specific molecular signal detection and classification workflow.
Complete a bioinformatics verification and analytical validation plan with predefined acceptance criteria.
Demonstrate reproducibility, robustness, and traceability across representative datasets, runs, and software configurations.
Deliver controlled technical documentation, automated testing, and versioned software releases.
Collaborate with assay development and clinical teams to support performance optimization and future clinical validation.

Core Competencies

Strong programming and statistical problem-solving skills.
Attention to detail and data integrity.
Ability to work with complex, high-dimensional biological datasets.
Effective cross-functional communication.
Ownership of technical deliverables and timelines.
Commitment to reproducible research, software quality, and patient safety.

Research Associate II / Senior Research Associate - Discovery Biology

Position Summary:

We are seeking a highly creative, passionate, and motivated individual to join us in developing the next generation of CRISPR-based therapeutics. This role is for a Research Associate II / Senior Research Associate I to join the XTID screening team within the Discovery Biology department, where you will support the advancement and scaling of gene-editing platform workflows through high-quality assay execution, optimization, and data generation.
In this position, you will apply strong hands-on expertise in cell-based and molecular assays to support arrayed screening workflows that characterize gene-editing molecules across relevant cell types and therapeutic contexts. You will execute and optimize experiments in plate-based formats, troubleshoot assay workflows, maintain rigorous documentation, and help improve assay robustness, throughput, and reproducibility.
The ideal candidate brings substantial bench experience in mammalian cell culture, plate-based assay execution, molecular biology, and quantitative data analysis. You should be comfortable working independently on defined experiments, organizing and prioritizing day-to-day activities across multiple concurrent projects, and maintaining exceptional attention to detail in sample tracking, documentation, and experimental execution. Success in this role requires strong organizational skills, effective time management, and the ability to consistently deliver high-quality data in a fast-paced environment.
Above all, you should have a genuine passion for developing next-generation CRISPR therapeutics and bring curiosity, scientific rigor, ownership, and a practical problem-solving mindset to help move these technologies from the bench toward the clinic.

Key Duties / Responsibilities:
Support the design, development, optimization, and validation of fit-for-purpose arrayed screening assays in 96-well and 384-well formats to characterize gene-editing molecules across multiple cell types and therapeutic contexts.
Execute high-throughput cell-based and biochemical assays with attention to robustness, reproducibility, and assay quality metrics such as CV, linearity, and signal window.
Produce mRNA via in vitro transcription to generate gene-editing materials for screening, ensuring quality, consistency, and scalability to meet program needs.
Formulate and produce lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for delivery of gene-editing cargo, optimizing formulation and process parameters for potency, reproducibility, and throughput.
Contribute to screening campaigns from experimental setup and sample processing through data capture, quality control, analysis, and interpretation of results.
Communicate experimental results, technical observations, and key findings to the team through presentations, and participation in team discussions.
Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot mammalian cell culture workflows, including immortalized, primary, iPSC-derived, and engineered cell models relevant to therapeutic programs.
Operate, help troubleshoot and refine laboratory automation and liquid-handling workflows to improve screening throughput, consistency, and scalability.
Maintain rigorous documentation in Benchling / LIMS systems and contribute to team best practices for assay robustness, reproducibility, sample tracking, and data quality.
Collaborate cross-functionally with scientists to ensure efficient coordination of experiments, sample processing, and data delivery.
Identify and troubleshoot assay or workflow issues, escalating risks appropriately and contributing practical improvements in performance, cost, and turnaround time.
Maintain strong organizational practices for sample management, reagent inventory, experiment scheduling, and data recording to ensure accurate execution of multiple concurrent projects.

Knowledge Requirements (Background/Skills/Experience):

BS/MS in Biology, Bioengineering, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, or a related discipline, with typically 4+ years of relevant hands-on experience supporting molecular and cell-based assay workflows
Strong hands-on experience executing and optimizing arrayed assays in plate-based formats (96-/384-well), including quantitative readouts such as NGS-based assays, fluorescence reporters, high-content imaging, ELISA, viability assays, RT-qPCR, or ddPCR.
Strong mammalian cell culture skills, including aseptic technique and experience with immortalized, primary, iPSC-derived, or engineered cell systems.
Working familiarity with core molecular biology methods such as cloning, CRISPR/gene editing, stable cell line generation, RT-qPCR, ddPCR, flow cytometry, and sample preparation for sequencing-based readouts.
Ability to clearly summarize experimental results, flag technical risks, and present decision-enabling data to scientific stakeholders while managing multiple experiments and timelines.
Demonstrated scientific rigor, strong organizational skills, and ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary team.
Preferred: familiarity with CRISPR therapeutic approaches, laboratory automation and liquid-handling platforms.

Most of your time (~ 70%) goes to analysis: building and owning reporting for our ministry partners, managing our internal data, and creating cross-ministry benchmarks. Approximately 20% is working with the people behind the requests. That means joining ministry partner calls when needed, finding out why someone is asking for a report, and coming back with more than they asked for.

What you'll do

Reporting and analysis (about 70%)

Client insight (about 20%)

Dig past the direct request: understand what led to it and where the ministry is headed.

Standardized reporting with benchmarks is running as a new service for our ministry partners, allowing them to see how their experience fits within a larger ministry context.

Position Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Bioinformatics Scientist or Senior Bioinformatics Scientist to develop, optimize, validate, and maintain bioinformatics pipelines for a cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening assay.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational biology, next-generation sequencing (NGS), molecular diagnostics, and statistical modeling. This individual will be responsible for transforming raw sequencing data into reliable analytical outputs and developing robust computational methods to identify cancer-associated molecular signals in plasma-derived cfDNA.

The role will support analytical validation, algorithm development, assay performance optimization, and preparation for clinical and regulatory submissions. The candidate will collaborate closely with molecular biology, assay development, laboratory automation, clinical, quality, and regulatory teams to establish a reproducible, scalable, and well-documented bioinformatics workflow.

Key Responsibilities

1. NGS Bioinformatics Pipeline Development

Develop, optimize, and maintain end-to-end bioinformatics pipelines for cfDNA-based targeted sequencing assays.
Process and analyze raw sequencing data, including FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, and VCF or other assay-specific intermediate files.
Implement quality control metrics for sequencing quality, mapping, coverage, library complexity, molecular error rates, and sample-level performance.
Develop methods for low-frequency variant detection, error suppression, background-noise characterization, and identification of cancer-associated molecular features, as appropriate to the assay design.
Optimize computational workflows for throughput, reproducibility, scalability, and efficient processing of high-volume sequencing data.
Integrate bioinformatics outputs with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), automated laboratory workflows, and downstream reporting systems as needed.

2. Algorithm and Biomarker Development

Develop and evaluate computational methods to identify cancer-associated signals in cfDNA, including genomic alterations and other molecular features supported by the assay design.
Collaborate with molecular biologists and assay scientists to investigate biological and technical sources of background noise.
Develop statistical models and classification algorithms to distinguish cancer-associated signals from non-cancer background.
Evaluate feature selection, model training, cross-validation, threshold optimization, and generalizability using appropriate study designs.
Assess the effects of cfDNA input, sequencing depth, tumor fraction, sample quality, and pre-analytical variables on algorithm performance.
Maintain clear separation between model development, parameter tuning, and independent performance evaluation to minimize overfitting and data leakage.

3. Bioinformatics Analytical Validation

Design and execute bioinformatics validation studies in collaboration with assay development and analytical validation teams.
Establish and document software and algorithm performance characteristics, including:
Analytical accuracy and reproducibility.
Detection performance across relevant signal levels.
False-positive and false-negative analytical calls.
Robustness to sequencing depth, input variability, and technical noise.
Sample-level quality control and failure criteria.
Computational precision, deterministic behavior, and reproducibility across software versions.
Evaluate the impact of sequencing errors, contamination, sample mix-ups, batch effects, and other potential confounders.
Define acceptance criteria, validation datasets, statistical analysis plans, and validation reports before study execution.
Support investigations of discrepant results, pipeline failures, and unexpected assay performance.

4. Software Engineering and Computational Infrastructure

Develop maintainable, modular, and version-controlled bioinformatics software using Python, R, and/or other appropriate programming languages.
Implement workflow management using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake, or WDL.
Use Git-based version control, automated testing, continuous integration, containers, and reproducible software environments.
Deploy workflows in cloud or high-performance computing environments, as appropriate.
Establish automated quality checks, audit-friendly execution logs, data lineage, version tracking, and monitoring.
Develop unit, integration, regression, and end-to-end tests to ensure reliable pipeline performance.
Collaborate with software engineering and IT teams to maintain secure and reliable computational infrastructure.

5. Clinical Performance and Translational Research Support

Support retrospective and prospective studies evaluating cfDNA-based cancer screening algorithms.
Collaborate with biostatisticians and clinical scientists to assess sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and other clinical performance measures.
Support the development of independent training, tuning, and test datasets for algorithm development and evaluation.
Analyze discordant cases and investigate associations between molecular features, clinical findings, and reference-standard outcomes.
Support clinical study data analysis, technical documentation, and preparation of scientific publications and presentations.

6. Regulatory, Quality, and Documentation

Prepare technical documentation for analytical validation, software verification and validation, design controls, and regulatory submissions.
Work with Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs to ensure compliance with applicable requirements for clinical laboratory testing and in vitro diagnostic software.
Maintain traceability between software requirements, risk controls, test cases, validation evidence, and software releases.
Contribute to change-control procedures, risk assessments, deviation investigations, and corrective and preventive actions when applicable.
Support the development of controlled procedures for pipeline deployment, updates, maintenance, and release approval.

7. Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with assay development, molecular biology, laboratory operations, automation engineering, biostatistics, clinical development, and regulatory teams.
Translate biological and clinical questions into computational analyses and actionable technical requirements.
Communicate complex bioinformatics findings clearly to scientific and non-computational stakeholders.
Contribute to experimental design, assay optimization, troubleshooting, and strategic development of the cancer screening platform.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Biostatistics, Computer Science, or a related discipline; alternatively, an M.S. with substantial relevant industry experience.
Strong experience analyzing NGS data, preferably from targeted sequencing assays or liquid biopsy applications.
Proficiency in Python and/or R, including experience developing reusable, well-tested analytical code.
Demonstrated understanding of NGS data processing, sequencing quality control, alignment, variant calling, and statistical analysis.
Experience with Linux/Unix environments, shell scripting, Git, and reproducible computational workflows.

Ability to independently troubleshoot complex computational problems and communicate results across multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing or validating bioinformatics pipelines for oncology or clinical diagnostics.

Reporting and analysis (about 70%)

Take over and improve RK's current reporting for ministry partners, including monthly financial reports, station data requests, and social media analytics reports.
Turn one-off client reports into a consistent RK reporting service that partners can rely on.
Fully own RK's cross-ministry benchmarks, with feedback from senior leadership: what "good" looks like by channel, and how each ministry compares.
Build those benchmarks into partner reports, so every ministry understands their experience in a broader context.
Manage and organize RK's internal data: understand what data we have, where it lives, and how to keep it clean and usable.
Present data-backed recommendations across various channels.

Client insight (about 20%)

Dig past the direct request: understand what led to it and where the ministry is headed.
Support the account lead in assessing how a report furthers a ministry’s impact.

Take part in internal team meetings, planning sessions, and company-wide meetings.
Keep building your skills through training, new tools, and learning the ministry media landscape, with RK’s support.

Other duties as assigned.

You'll work mainly with the Media Services team, which includes Station Relations and Digital Marketing. Over time there's room to grow into work with all of our teams.

You know our ministry partners, their goals, and the reports we provide each of them.

You've mapped what data RK has, where it lives, who owns it, and how it's collected.
You've joined client calls with the Media Services team and built working relationships with the account leads.

You've set up how client data is organized and protected, so cross-ministry benchmarking can be done responsibly.
Account leads bring you into client conversations because your recommendations go beyond the original request.

Standardized reporting with benchmarks is running as a new service for our ministry partners, allowing them to see how their experience fits within a larger ministry context. 
RK's data and reporting processes are documented and repeatable.
You’ve elevated reporting both internally and for our clients.
